narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist; narrating the questions put to Jesus in the temple.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; telling the parable of the marriage feast, then answering each trap with calm authority.

pharisees-and-herodians.name: Pharisees and Herodians
pharisees-and-herodians.note: Disciples of the Pharisees with the Herodians, sent to trap him over the tribute; smooth, flattering, insincere.

sadducees.name: The Sadducees
sadducees.note: Sadducees, who deny the resurrection; posing their riddle with sceptical, faintly mocking confidence.

scribe-who-asks.name: The doctor of the law who asks about the great commandment
scribe-who-asks.note: A Pharisee, a doctor of the law; here putting his question as a test.

pharisees.name: The Pharisees
pharisees.note: The Pharisees gathered together; a short, confident answer.

1.t: And Jesus answering, spoke again in parables to them, saying:

2.t: The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king who made a marriage for his son.

3.t: And he sent his servants to call them that were invited to the marriage: and they would not come.

4.t: Again he sent other servants, saying: Tell them that were invited, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my beeves and fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come ye to the marriage.

5.t: But they neglected and went their ways, one to his farm and another to his merchandise.

6.t: And the rest laid hands on his servants and, having treated them contumeliously, put them to death.

7.t: But when the king had heard of it, he was angry: and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers and burnt their city.

8.t: Then he saith to his servants: The marriage indeed is ready; but they that were invited were not worthy.

9.t: Go ye therefore into the highways; and as many as you shall find, call to the marriage.

10.t: And his servants going forth into the ways, gathered together all that they found, both bad and good: and the marriage was filled with guests.

11.t: And the king went in to see the guests: and he saw there a man who had not on a wedding garment.

12.t: And he saith to him: Friend, how camest thou in hither not having on a wedding garment? But he was silent.

13.t: Then the king said to the waiters: Bind his hands and feet, and cast him into the exterior darkness. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

14.t: For many are called, but few are chosen.

15.t: Then the Pharisees going, consulted among themselves how to insnare him in his speech.

16.t: And they sent to him their disciples with the Herodians, saying:
Master, we know that thou art a true speaker and teachest the way of God in truth. Neither carest thou for any man: for thou dost not regard the person of men.

17.t: Tell us therefore what dost thou think? Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

18.t: But Jesus knowing their wickedness, said:
Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites?

19.t: Shew me the coin of the tribute.
And they offered him a penny.

20.t: Whose image and inscription is this?

21.t: Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's; and to God, the things that are God's.

22.t: And hearing this, they wondered and, leaving him, went their ways.

23.t: That day there came to him the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection; and asked him,

24.t: Master, Moses said: If a man die having no son, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up issue to his brother.

25.t: Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first having married a wife, died; and not having issue, left his wife to his brother.

26.t: In like manner the second and the third and so on, to the seventh.

27.t: And last of all the woman died also.

28.t: At the resurrection therefore, whose wife of the seven shall she be? For they all had her.

29.t: And Jesus answering, said to them:
You err, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.

30.t: For in the resurrection they shall neither marry nor be married, but shall be as the angels of God in heaven.

31.t: And concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that which was spoken by God, saying to you:

32.t: I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob? He is not the God of the dead but of the living.

33.t: And the multitudes hearing it were in admiration at his doctrine.

34.t: But the Pharisees, hearing that he had silenced the Sadducees, came together.

35.t: And one of them, a doctor of the law, asked him, tempting him:

36.t: Master, which is the great commandment in the law?
36.q: Matthew's doctor of the law is the scribe of Mark 12:28 (same question, same place); Mark's id kept rather than `lawyer`

37.t: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart and with thy whole soul and with thy whole mind.

38.t: This is the greatest and the first commandment.

39.t: And the second is like to this: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

40.t: On these two commandments dependeth the whole law and the prophets.

41.t: And the Pharisees being gathered together, Jesus asked them,

42.t: What think you of Christ? Whose son is he?

43.t: How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying:

44.t: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit on my right hand, until I make thy enemies thy footstool?

45.t: If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?

46.t: And no man was able to answer him a word: neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.
